Choose how to open the in-game settings panel: a draggable floating icon, or a swipe-from-edge drawer.

On some devices the edge-swipe drawer may not respond, leaving you stuck on the overlay with no way to close it from inside the game. The floating icon is the recommended option. Continue with the drawer?

Hosts the overlay as a trusted accessibility surface so taps reach the app underneath on strict devices (e.g. Orange Pi 5 Ultra) where they would otherwise be blocked. Trade-off: while a session is running the overlay covers the status bar and navigation bar — you cannot pull down notifications or tap home/back. Leave OFF if your device passes taps already; turn ON only when you cannot tap through. Requires the LSFG-Android+ accessibility service to be enabled.

Extra fallback for the rare device where taps still don\'t reach the game even with trusted overlay on. The accessibility service replays the touch directly instead of relying on pass-through. Only take this if trusted overlay alone didn\'t fix tapping — enabling it when pass-through already works can cause duplicate taps.
MediaProjection captures through Android screen sharing. Shizuku and Root capture use a privileged UID-filtered target capture path, useful on devices whose MediaProjection includes overlays.
Show a live plot of generated frame intervals in the overlay. Useful for diagnosing stutter.

Lossless.dll runs the Vulkan LSFG shader pipeline. AI model (ncnn) runs the FlowNetLite/RefineNetLite interpolator you trained and exported from the notebook. Only the active backend\'s source needs to be ready to start a session.

rife-v4.25-lite_ensembleFalse ships built into the app (assets/models/) — there\'s nothing to pick or import. Precision is fixed at FP16, baked into the shipped weights; the toggle below only controls where inference runs (GPU vs CPU), not precision.
Number of frames produced per real frame. 2 = one interpolated frame between each pair. 3–4 recommended on mobile.
Internal motion estimation resolution. Lower = faster but less accurate.

Percentage of the display\'s native resolution to capture and render at. Lower values cut GPU cost across capture and frame-gen, at the cost of a softer image. Takes effect on the next capture (re)start.

Limits how many incoming capture frames are admitted into the pipeline at all. Frames arriving faster than this rate are dropped before capture handling, blit, and frame generation — the whole pipeline runs at the capped rate, saving power (e.g. capping a 60fps game to 30 processes ~30fps and feeds that into frame generation instead of 60). 0 = unlimited. Takes effect on the next capture (re)start.

Unlike Input FPS cap above (which only throttles what we admit into our own pipeline), this tries to steer the game\'s own render rate toward the target by competing for CPU headroom: when the game is measured running above target, we widen onto the performance CPU cluster to compete for it; when it\'s at or below target, we pull back to efficiency cores to hand headroom back so the game can climb. Useful alongside frame generation — e.g. lock a 60fps game to 30-40 to save power and free up headroom before multiplying with frame gen. Best-effort and device-dependent: it competes for CPU, not GPU, so results vary by device and by whether the game is CPU- or GPU-bound. 0 = disabled.
Use the faster, lower-quality shader variant. Recommended on mid-range GPUs.
Enable only if your device and game output HDR.

Use the half-precision shader variants pre-compiled inside Lossless.dll instead of the full-precision FP32 set. Reduces GPU load and memory bandwidth. Quality is virtually identical; falls back to FP32 automatically if anything goes wrong.
Show a small FPS readout in the top-left of the overlay. MediaProjection counts visible capture frames; Shizuku capture counts privileged UID-filtered target frames.
Choose where the in-game drawer handle appears on the overlay.

Pick the apps that should automatically show the LSFG-Android+ launcher when opened from the home screen. A small floating icon appears on top of the game; tap it to start the frame-generation overlay.
Enable the LSFG-Android+ accessibility service so the app can detect when one of the selected games is opened.

On non-rooted Android, LSFG-Android+ cannot be injected into another app\'s Vulkan context like on Linux. MediaProjection provides the standard capture path; Shizuku capture can use a privileged UID-filtered target path on supported builds and requires Shizuku with ADB or wireless debugging active. See the README for details.
